newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Skoda says signs assembly deal in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Skoda says signs assembly deal in Russia.

text.p: Volkswagen AG Czech unit Skoda Automobilova a.s. said on Wednesday that it had signed an agreement with a partner in the city of Smolensk west of Moscow to assemble Skoda cars in Russia.
"The partner firm is from Smolensk," spokesman Milan Smutny told Reuters by telephone from Skoda headquarters in the Czech city of Mlada Boleslav.
He declined to name the partner involved but said it would be revealed when production begins later this year.
Smutny said a majority of the "hundreds of cars" produced initially in the Russian venture would be Skoda's flagship compact line, the Felicia. Further details were not disclosed.
The company has been searching for a deal to utilise existing factories lying idle due to economic reform in Russia.

In November, Skoda said it was hoping to sell 10,000 of its Felicia and mid-size Octavia models in Russia in 1997, twice last year's sales, but most would be from its existing factory in the Czech town of Mlada Boleslav.
Selling Czech-made cars on the Russian market has been difficult with tariffs of between 80 and 100 percent added to the price.
Skoda said it planned to follow the model of its assembly plant in the Polish city of Poznan, where 16,000 Skoda's were to be made in 1996, rising to 30,000 in 1997.
